title: Build the shared e2e test harness and NDJSON logging library
description:
GOAL
Create scripts/e2e/lib.sh (structured-logging bash library), scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (discovers and runs every scripts/e2e/*.sh test, aggregates NDJSON logs, prints a machine-readable summary), and the conventions every later e2e subtask in this graph builds on.

WHY / BACKGROUND
Every vertical slice in this project must prove itself with end-to-end evidence, and the constitution requires that evidence to be replayable and machine-inspectable — a wall of unstructured stdout is not evidence. One shared harness means every e2e script logs identically, failures always carry enough context to replay (seeds, digests, exact commands), and run_all.sh becomes the single local entry point the verify.sh `full` lane will eventually call instead of its current typed dormant refusal (exit 3).

DELIVERABLES
- scripts/e2e/lib.sh: step(), assert_eq(), assert_file_digest(), with_seed(), log-to-NDJSON functions; every step line carries ts/script/step/cmd/exit/duration_ms/artifact_digests/seed/note.
- scripts/e2e/run_all.sh: runs all scripts/e2e/*.sh except lib, collects per-script NDJSON into e2e-logs/<timestamp>/, emits a summary JSON {scripts, steps, passed, failed, wall_ms}, exit nonzero on any failure.
- A trivial self-test script scripts/e2e/harness_selftest.sh exercising every lib function including the failure path (run in a subshell so the suite still passes).
- Documentation of the conventions in a comment header of lib.sh (the canonical reference; no separate doc to drift).

ACCEPTANCE
- harness_selftest.sh passes and demonstrably exercises the failure path with the context dump;
- run_all.sh aggregates >=1 script and its summary JSON parses with python3 -m json.tool;
- logs are valid NDJSON (each line parses independently);
- shellcheck-clean or explicitly annotated; bash -n clean; set -euo pipefail everywhere;
- ./scripts/verify.sh fast stays green (the harness adds no Rust surface).

NON-GOALS
- No test content for real subsystems here (later beads own that); no CI wiring (workflow YAML stays a thin adapter).

FUTURE-SELF NOTES
The full/release lanes must keep refusing (exit 3) until real engine lanes exist — do NOT wire run_all.sh into verify.sh full as a green path while the suite is trivial; that would be exactly the false-green NEG-012 rejects.

CONSTITUTIONAL CONSTRAINTS (AGENTS.md; non-negotiable)
- Pure Rust, edition 2024, dated-nightly pin from rust-toolchain.toml; every first-party crate carries #![forbid(unsafe_code)]; no C/C++ FFI, no C Git/libgit2/JGit/Dulwich/gix, no hidden subprocess fallback. Upstream Git binaries are pinned, sandboxed differential ORACLES only (never production).
- Asupersync is the sole async runtime (no Tokio/async-std/smol). Long-lived work owns children via regions; cancellation is request -> drain -> finalize; effects use typed obligations (Reserved -> Committed -> Acknowledged, or Reserved -> Aborted).
- Closed dependency universe: every crate (incl. transitive, enforced via Cargo.lock scan) must match an active allow row in registries/dependency_policy.tsv. No build scripts/proc macros without a constitutional exception. No network during builds.
- Final-abstraction slices only: no empty crates, no HashMap-pretending-to-be-storage, no fixture-only parser wired as production API. A subset is fine when its unsupported surface is a typed refusal.
- Claim lattice (invariant > proof > bounded model > statistical > SLO > benchmark): never describe this work as stronger than its evidence. Record disproven hypotheses in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE_LEDGER.md + registries/negative_evidence.tsv.
- Run ./scripts/verify.sh fast before and after; stage only intended files; keep generated artifacts out of source.

E2E LOGGING CONVENTIONS (mandatory for every e2e script)
- Scripts live in scripts/e2e/, are bash with `set -euo pipefail`, and source scripts/e2e/lib.sh (built by the e2e-harness bead).
- Every step emits one NDJSON line to the log file AND stderr: {"ts":..., "script":..., "step":..., "cmd":..., "exit":..., "duration_ms":..., "artifact_digests":{...}, "seed":..., "note":...}.
- Assertions log expected vs actual on failure and dump the relevant state directory listing + last 50 log lines of the process under test before exiting nonzero.
- Deterministic seeds are logged and settable via env so any failure replays exactly.
- A final summary line reports steps run/passed/failed and total wall time; exit code is the number of failed steps capped at 1.

---
## PLAN-SPACE REVIEW REVISIONS (added during the pre-implementation polish pass)

- Add acceptance/cross-reference: a follow-up bead (fg091-release-gate) OWNS wiring run_all.sh into verify.sh full/release; this bead's FUTURE-SELF deferral is discharged only when fg091 exists (it now does).

title: Build the pinned upstream-Git differential-oracle harness
description:
GOAL
A sandboxed harness that downloads/pins exact upstream Git versions (recorded by version + binary digest), runs them ONLY in conformance lanes, captures byte-level transcripts (pkt-line exchanges, pack bytes, exit codes, stderr classes), and provides a comparison library that diffs FrankenGit behavior against oracle behavior with typed classifications (byte-equal / semantically-equal-declared / divergent).

WHY / BACKGROUND
The constitution forbids upstream Git in any production path but REQUIRES it as the differential oracle for compatibility claims (AGENTS.md §6; dependency_policy.tsv DEP-012 external_oracle). Every Git-facing slice (object core, pack reader/writer, upload-pack, receive-pack, the e2e slice) needs the same pinned-oracle machinery; building it once prevents each slice from inventing its own slightly-different comparison semantics — which is how false compatibility claims are born.

DELIVERABLES
- tools/git-oracle/ scripts: fetch-and-pin (records url, version, sha256 into a checked-in pin manifest), sandbox-run wrapper (no network, temp HOME, explicit env allowlist), transcript capture (client<->server byte logs), and compare library emitting NDJSON verdicts.
- Pin manifest format documented in-file; at least two pinned Git versions (one older, one current) because negotiation behavior differs across versions and the compatibility matrix declares per-version targets.
- Integration with the e2e harness logging conventions (fg000a).

ACCEPTANCE
- Harness runs a pinned Git binary fully sandboxed (no network, no user config leakage — proven by a probe test);
- transcripts are reproducible byte-for-byte for a deterministic fixture repo;
- comparison verdicts are typed and machine-readable, never a bare diff dump;
- the pin manifest records exact digests and the harness refuses a binary whose digest mismatches (fail closed);
- nothing under tools/git-oracle/ is reachable from production code (no Cargo dependency edge; shell/tooling only).

NON-GOALS
- No conformance corpus content here (owned by the Git-slice beads); no CI execution.

FUTURE-SELF NOTES

title: FG-001 completion: emit verification replay artifacts from local lanes
description:
GOAL
Complete the last open acceptance item of backlog FG-001 (the constitutional registries + checker are already implemented and green): every ./scripts/verify.sh lane run emits a replay artifact recording source tree state (HEAD + dirty-file digest), toolchain (rustc -V), exact command, exit code, duration, and a digest of the checker report.

WHY / BACKGROUND
FG-001's other acceptance items landed with fgit-registry-check (registries reject duplicate/unsorted IDs, bad schemas, unknown statuses; unsafe/FFI/foreign-Git/build-script violations fail closed; links/fences/TxId-uniqueness/workflow rules are mechanical). What is missing is the EVIDENCE side: a green run currently leaves no artifact, so a claim that "the lane passed at revision X" is unverifiable prose — precisely what the claim lattice forbids. The replay artifact is the smallest unit of the evidence-envelope discipline (plan §34.1) applied to our own tooling.

DELIVERABLES
- verify.sh writes evidence/verify/<utc-timestamp>-<lane>.json (git-ignored directory; evidence/ added to .gitignore) with: lane, command line, HEAD commit, dirty status + digest-of-diff, rustc/cargo versions, exit code, wall time, and sha256 of captured stdout+stderr.
- --no-artifact escape hatch for tight loops; artifact writing must never change the lane exit code (failure to write = warning to stderr).
- The artifact schema documented in a comment in verify.sh (single source).

ACCEPTANCE

title: Checker: implement version-universe and constellation.lock verification
description:
GOAL
Implement the closed-world version-universe and constellation.lock gate before any FrankenSuite sibling enters a release-facing FrankenGit graph.

WHY / BACKGROUND
Asupersync is the sole runtime and its Cx/Outcome/Budget types are part of protocol ownership, not a replaceable executor detail. Cargo may legally resolve multiple incompatible 0.x versions, but FrankenGit may not. The adopted fastapi_rust, sqlmodel_rust, FrankenTUI, FrankenSQLite, and Asupersync revisions must converge upstream before integration; the framework choices are settled, while the gate remains fail-closed until one exact constellation exists.

REVIEWED 2026-08-20 SNAPSHOT (evidence, not final pins)
- Asupersync 0.4.9 at 9eb0600e6ef4d17633dff3dc43ad99c64e72adbe.
- FrankenSQLite 0.3.7 at f99d639b019c1400e55135c8ee4ba988f2587df9, requiring Asupersync >=0.4.3,<0.5.
- fastapi_rust at 531456a62e4484d74378c7f99b822eacae66043d currently requires Asupersync 0.3.9.
- sqlmodel_rust at 23da90cdfe057162d436417bbc4af7ec206ed48e currently pins Asupersync =0.4.4 and contains absolute local FrankenSQLite patches.
- FrankenTUI at a136062fa3e4f325a45414d00f35e39a0de27870 currently requires Asupersync 0.3.9 for its executor feature.
These sibling projects will be updated by their owner. FrankenGit must wait for and verify those updates; it must not resolve two runtimes, substitute another framework, or commit local paths.

DELIVERABLES
- constellation.lock schema binding exact source/version/revision, checksum, enabled/default-disabled features, public-contract fingerprint, target support class, license, build scripts, proc macros, transitive-unsafe digest, evidence class, and removal/update path;
- Cargo.lock and cargo-metadata checker proving one Asupersync version/type universe, one compatible FrankenSuite constellation, registry-resolvable release sources, and exact feature closure;
- explicit rejection of absolute/relative unpublished path dependencies, [patch]/[replace] in release-facing manifests, alternate runtimes, forbidden backend crates, unregistered features, and source drift;
- candidate-to-admitted workflow that records why every upstream convergence prerequisite is satisfied without describing compilation alone as admission.

ACCEPTANCE
- active-but-vacuous pass is explicit while no sibling is linked;
- planted fixtures fail for: second Asupersync version, Tokio, version/source/checksum drift, missing constellation row, unexpected default feature, absolute path, [patch]/[replace], forbidden sqlmodel backend, ftui demo/showcase closure, build-script/proc-macro drift, and missing unsafe/license evidence;
- exact post-update adopted stack resolves one Asupersync 0.4.x and one admitted FrankenSQLite release, or remains blocked with a typed diagnostic naming the sibling prerequisite;
- no hard-coded issue/test counts; the checker derives required rows from manifests and Cargo.lock;
- unit tests cover schema parsing and every diagnostic; scripts/e2e/constellation_gate.sh runs the planted-negative matrix with step-level NDJSON and is registered in the exact suite manifest.

E2E LOGGING
The script sources scripts/e2e/lib.sh, uses set -euo pipefail, emits one NDJSON record per step to stderr and its artifact log, records source/toolchain/lock/constellation digests, command, exit, duration, fixture, expected/actual diagnostic, and final totals, and preserves a replay command on failure.

CONSTITUTIONAL CONSTRAINTS
Pure Rust and #![forbid(unsafe_code)] for every first-party crate; no first-party exception, C/C++ FFI, production Git subprocess, alternate runtime, network build, or unpublished path. Transitive/generated unsafe is pinned and ledgered. Run repository-owned verification locally and keep this bead blocked rather than weakening the architecture.

---
## PLAN-SPACE REVIEW REVISIONS (added during the pre-implementation polish pass)

### BINDING INTEGRATION PROFILE: docs/ASUPERSYNC_AND_FRANKENSQLITE_INTEGRATION_PROFILE.md is authoritative

This bead's constellation gate enforces §1 and §6 of that profile:
- Reviewed planning snapshot (must be re-audited live and pinned in constellation.lock): Asupersync 0.4.9, FrankenSQLite 0.3.7 (asupersync >=0.4.3,<0.5, default-features off at the edge), fastapi_rust (asupersync 0.3.9), sqlmodel_rust (asupersync =0.4.4, with local absolute [patch] entries that MUST be removed), FrankenTUI (asupersync-executor requires 0.3.9). The fastapi/ftui 0.3.9 vs sqlmodel 0.4.4 skew is the exact thing this gate must resolve to ONE Asupersync revision.
- Hard rule: two Asupersync versions are two runtime/type universes even if Cargo resolves both — "the resolver found a build" is NOT an admission result. The gate closes only after repository-owned probes compile every exact feature closure against ONE selected Asupersync and the checker verifies the resulting lockfile.
- §6 fail-closed admission/stop conditions (any one blocks integration): >1 Asupersync or any Tokio/other executor; unpublished/absolute path dependency or build-time network; first-party unsafe/FFI/native-db/lint-exception; a path that cannot accept a runtime-owned Cx + finite budget + explicit cancellation + quiescent close; an unproven concurrency/restart/browser/durability support-class claim; or a db/model/projection result becoming authority. A failed gate names the required sibling update; it never authorizes a substitute framework.
- Add acceptance (constellation-probe e2e, §5.2): plant a second Asupersync, a Tokio, an absolute-path [patch], a forbidden backend, an unsafe/build-script/proc-macro drift, and an unsupported feature — each must fail the gate typed.

### WASM adapter unsafe (reconciled): transitive surface, not an exception

The client WASM UI introduces NO first-party unsafe exception. wasm-bindgen and framework crates that emit/link unsafe are ordinary transitive dependency surface subject to the closed-dependency + unsafe-ledger gates (fg001c): pinned, audited, feature-bounded, ledgered. The first-party browser adapter crate stays `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`. If a WASM framework cannot satisfy that, integration is blocked pending an owned-upstream correction — the gate never resolves a first-party unsafe waiver.

title: Checker: empty-crate/placeholder detection and transitive-unsafe ledger
FG-002: Freeze canonical codec, crypto registry, and typed identities
description:
GOAL
One canonical byte-encoding profile for every immutable FrankenGit body, a versioned domain-separated digest/crypto registry, and typed algorithm-agile identities — without ever rewriting or aliasing native Git OIDs.

WHY / BACKGROUND
Everything downstream — seals, capsules, decisions, RCRs, batches, heads, evidence — derives identity from canonical bytes. If two encoders can produce different bytes for "the same" value, identity splits and the whole authority model (one TxId, one terminal outcome, one head chain) collapses. This is why the plan (§11) demands one deterministic encoding, explicit version/domain/algorithm, canonical ordering, bounded decoding, and golden vectors, and why exactly ONE TxId derivation may exist repo-wide (mechanically enforced by fgit-registry-check). Native Git identity is (GitHashAlgorithm, digest bytes): SHA-1 and SHA-256 are distinct TYPES, never compared by bytes; internal strong digests add evidence but never replace or upgrade Git OIDs (plan §11.2/§11.6).

DESIGN DECISIONS TO MAKE HERE (plan §47 D1)
Compare hand-owned binary framing vs postcard/CBOR-like subsets vs purpose-built codec on: one-byte-string-per-value, bounded decoding, WASM portability, forward compatibility, auditability. Decision lands as an ADR with alternatives and non-claims. No floats, no ambiguous-order maps, no platform-sized integers, no locale, no wall-clock identity inputs.

STRUCTURE
This epic closes when its three subtasks (encoding+goldens; digest/crypto registry; adversarial corpus + independent verifier) are closed and the combined evidence exists.

ACCEPTANCE (epic-level)
- domain/version/length framing and unknown-field rules specified and implemented in fgit-types/fgit-codec;
- unsigned-body vs signature/attestation envelope convention fixed (signatures NEVER inside identity bytes — plan §14.1 precedent);
- SHA-1/SHA-256 Git OIDs remain distinct types from all internal IDs; no API accepts an untyped hash string where two domains are possible;
- golden valid/invalid vectors checked in; independent minimal verifier (separate crate or std-only test binary) validates them;
- algorithm registry supports migration/mixed-version without confusing native Git IDs;
- mutation corpus proves noncanonical encodings never share an identity with canonical ones.

FUTURE-SELF NOTES
This is the deepest possible foundation: get it wrong and every later golden vector churns. Freeze slowly, test violently. The workspace crates here (fgit-types, fgit-codec) are the first engine crates — they must arrive as real vertical slices with tests, not scaffolds (fg001c tripwire will also enforce this).

CONSTITUTIONAL CONSTRAINTS (AGENTS.md; non-negotiable)
- Pure Rust, edition 2024, dated-nightly pin from rust-toolchain.toml; every first-party crate carries #![forbid(unsafe_code)]; no C/C++ FFI, no C Git/libgit2/JGit/Dulwich/gix, no hidden subprocess fallback. Upstream Git binaries are pinned, sandboxed differential ORACLES only (never production).
- Asupersync is the sole async runtime (no Tokio/async-std/smol). Long-lived work owns children via regions; cancellation is request -> drain -> finalize; effects use typed obligations (Reserved -> Committed -> Acknowledged, or Reserved -> Aborted).
- Closed dependency universe: every crate (incl. transitive, enforced via Cargo.lock scan) must match an active allow row in registries/dependency_policy.tsv. No build scripts/proc macros without a constitutional exception. No network during builds.
- Final-abstraction slices only: no empty crates, no HashMap-pretending-to-be-storage, no fixture-only parser wired as production API. A subset is fine when its unsupported surface is a typed refusal.
- Claim lattice (invariant > proof > bounded model > statistical > SLO > benchmark): never describe this work as stronger than its evidence. Record disproven hypotheses in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE_LEDGER.md + registries/negative_evidence.tsv.
- Run ./scripts/verify.sh fast before and after; stage only intended files; keep generated artifacts out of source.

---
## EMBEDDED NORMATIVE CONTENT (verbatim from the design docs; self-contained — do not consult the source markdown)

### Canonical identity rules (NORMATIVE_PROTOCOL_CONTRACTS §3, §11)

- A Git object identity is `(GitHashAlgorithm, digest_bytes)`. SHA-1 and SHA-256 are DISTINCT TYPES/domains even if bytes/hex resemble one another. FrankenGit preserves the repository's native object format and never synthesizes cross-format equality (release-blocking invariant 12: "SHA-1 and SHA-256 cannot collide at the type boundary").
- Internal immutable IDs use a domain-separated canonical-envelope rule and a versioned cryptographic registry. The typed ID carries algorithm, object domain, canonical-codec version, and digest bytes. Storage path, mutable placement acknowledgement, transport framing, and signatures are EXCLUDED from identity unless a schema explicitly makes them logical content.
- There is exactly one normative derivation of the logical transaction identity `TxId` (the checker enforces that the `TxId = H(...)` formula appears in exactly one file, NORMATIVE_PROTOCOL_CONTRACTS). Ingress canonicalizes every semantically relevant field BEFORE deriving `TxId`; a network `RequestId` is tracing only.
- Every identity-bearing schema has: one deterministic byte encoding; explicit version/domain/algorithm; canonical integer/string/map ordering and normalization; bounded decoder and unknown-version behavior; golden vectors across native/WASM targets; collision/domain-separation tests; migration and mixed-version rules. No API accepts an untyped "hash string" where multiple identity domains are possible.
- No floats, ambiguous-order maps, platform-sized integers, locale, or wall-clock as identity inputs.

title: FG-002b: Domain-separated digest/crypto registry and typed OIDs
description:
SCOPE (subtask of fg002-canonical-codec)
The versioned cryptographic registry: algorithm IDs, object-domain separation tags, typed internal ID = (algorithm, domain, codec version, digest bytes); typed native Git OIDs (SHA-1 and SHA-256 as distinct types) kept strictly apart from internal IDs.

WHY THIS SHAPE: domain separation prevents a digest of one object class being replayed as another class (a real cross-protocol attack class); typing prevents the silent SHA-1/SHA-256 byte-aliasing the compatibility matrix explicitly bans. SHA-1 collision defense (plan §11.6): collision-detecting SHA-1 path for Git identity, strong internal payload commitment alongside, fail closed on collision evidence, never invisibly upgrade old signatures.

ACCEPTANCE
- creating an internal ID without a domain tag is unrepresentable in the API;
- cross-domain digest replay produces a typed mismatch in tests;
- Git OID types reject cross-format comparison at compile time; hex parsing requires explicit algorithm context;
- collision-defense hook point exists with a test double (real sha1cd selection is a dependency-registry decision recorded when made);
- registry rows for every algorithm/domain live in code as a closed enum + are exported into the golden corpus so fg002c's independent verifier can check them.

title: FG-002c: Codec mutation/adversarial corpus + independent verifier
description:
SCOPE (subtask of fg002-canonical-codec; test/evidence slice)
An adversarial campaign proving identity cannot be confused: mutation corpus (bit flips, truncations, extensions, reordered fields, duplicated fields, wrong domain tags, wrong versions) over every golden vector, asserting each mutant either decodes to a DIFFERENT identity or refuses — never the same identity; plus an INDEPENDENT minimal verifier (std-only, sharing no code with fgit-codec beyond type definitions) that re-derives digests for all goldens.

WHY INDEPENDENT: a bug shared by encoder and checker is invisible; independence is the point (same doctrine as verifier-independence classes in the agent protocol).

title: FG-004: AuthorityStore contract, in-memory faultable profile, and history checker
description:
GOAL
The backend-neutral primitive set on which ALL canonical publication rests: strong put-if-absent (seals, immutable bodies), authenticated head read with exact version token, and conditional head replacement (CAS) with monotone generation — specified as a trait (crate fgit-authority), implemented by an in-memory faultable reference backend, and policed by a linearizability history checker.

WHY / BACKGROUND
The entire v3 architecture removed leader/lease/home-cell correctness (NEG-013) and put ALL ordering authority into one conditional primitive. Therefore the primitive's contract must be airtight: ABA protection (a byte-identical restored body must NOT satisfy a CAS expecting the old incarnation — this is exactly the S3 content-derived-ETag hazard, plan §8.5/OSDL), no correctness dependence on listings/notifications/clocks/lease expiry, and read-your-writes for the head key. Backends earn trust ONLY by passing this suite — "S3-compatible" is marketing, not semantics (risk R3).

STRUCTURE: subtasks = (a) trait + contract spec + in-memory faultable impl, (b) linearizability history schema + checker, (c) fault suite.

ACCEPTANCE (epic)
- trait covers put-if-absent, read-with-version-token, conditional-replace-exact-token, monotone generation exposure; explicitly NO list/scan operation in the trait;
- in-memory profile supports scripted fault injection (duplicate responses, lost acks, delayed/stale reads, ambiguous CAS outcomes) for the lab (FG-013 consumes this);
- history checker validates linearizability of recorded histories and rejects seeded violations;
- explicit typed refusal path for backends that cannot prove the contract (used by the future object-store adapter FG-006).

FUTURE-SELF NOTES
Ambiguous CAS response (timeout after send) is NORMAL — the resolution is reread + outcome lookup by TxId, never assume-failed. Encode that in the contract docs and tests now, because every retry bug in the future traces back to this seam.

- Pure Rust, edition 2024, dated-nightly pin from rust-toolchain.toml; every first-party crate carries #![forbid(unsafe_code)]; no C/C++ FFI, no C Git/libgit2/JGit/Dulwich/gix, no hidden subprocess fallback. Upstream Git binaries are pinned, sandboxed differential ORACLES only (never production).
- Asupersync is the sole async runtime (no Tokio/async-std/smol). Long-lived work owns children via regions; cancellation is request -> drain -> finalize; effects use typed obligations (Reserved -> Committed -> Acknowledged, or Reserved -> Aborted).
- Closed dependency universe: every crate (incl. transitive, enforced via Cargo.lock scan) must match an active allow row in registries/dependency_policy.tsv. No build scripts/proc macros without a constitutional exception. No network during builds.
- Final-abstraction slices only: no empty crates, no HashMap-pretending-to-be-storage, no fixture-only parser wired as production API. A subset is fine when its unsupported surface is a typed refusal.
- Claim lattice (invariant > proof > bounded model > statistical > SLO > benchmark): never describe this work as stronger than its evidence. Record disproven hypotheses in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE_LEDGER.md + registries/negative_evidence.tsv.
- Run ./scripts/verify.sh fast before and after; stage only intended files; keep generated artifacts out of source.

---
## EMBEDDED NORMATIVE CONTENT (verbatim from the design docs; self-contained — do not consult the source markdown)

### AuthorityStore contract (plan §9.4 / OBJECT_STORE_DECISION_LOG) — earns trust only by conformance

Primitives: strong put-if-absent (seals, immutable bodies); authenticated head read with EXACT version token; conditional head replacement (CAS) with monotone generation. NO list/scan operation participates in truth or recovery (recovery follows known keys from authenticated roots, never bucket listings). ABA defense: version tokens must be UNIQUE PER WRITE — a byte-identical restored body must NOT satisfy a CAS expecting the old incarnation (the exact hazard of content-derived S3 ETags); the head body's monotone generation is an independent check. Ambiguous CAS response (timeout after send) is NORMAL control flow — resolve by reread + outcome-lookup by TxId, NEVER assume-failed. Deployment profiles (embedded FrankenSQLite / object-store / future fgit-authorityd) all pass the SAME conformance + linearizability + fault suite; a backend that cannot prove the contract refuses startup (fail closed). "S3-compatible" by product name does not establish CAS semantics (plan §8.5).

---
## PLAN-SPACE REVIEW REVISIONS (added during the pre-implementation polish pass)

### INTEGRATION PROFILE note (§3.4 commit-guard honesty)

The embedded FrankenSQLite authority backend serializes part of commit validation/write/publication through a commit guard (docs/ASUPERSYNC_AND_FRANKENSQLITE_INTEGRATION_PROFILE.md §3.4). FrankenGit may exploit parallel preparation and concurrent readers, but the AuthorityStore contract and its conformance suite must NOT claim lock-free or unconstrained multi-writer commit — the single-CAS linearization point stands, and throughput claims are bounded to the proven concurrency envelope (§3.5).

title: FG-005: Embedded FrankenSQLite authority profile
FG-005a: FrankenSQLite AuthorityStore implementation
FG-005b: FrankenSQLite profile crash matrix and reference equivalence
FG-006: Object-store AuthorityStore conformance adapter
description:
GOAL
One provider-neutral adapter exposing the exact AuthorityStore contract over an object-store API (conditional writes / If-Match-class semantics), with the conformance evidence that separates provable backends from marketing.

WHY / BACKGROUND
Hosted/clustered FrankenGit keeps truth in an object store (Cursor-derived insight), but risk R3 is real: nominally S3-compatible backends differ on linearizability, version tokens, gateways, and failover. The adapter must verify version/ETag/conditional semantics EMPIRICALLY per backend and refuse startup on unprovable semantics (fail closed, never degrade silently). ABA: content-derived ETags make byte-identical restores satisfy stale If-Match — so the head body must carry the monotone generation as an independent check, and the adapter must detect and reject token-reuse anomalies.

STRUCTURE: subtasks = (a) adapter over a minimal owned HTTP/signing surface (Asupersync-based, no cloud SDK — DEP-010), (b) Jepsen-style fault campaign using the FG-004b checker.

ACCEPTANCE (epic)
- capability receipt records exact API/region/configuration probed;
- concurrent histories over injected faults pass the linearizability checker for a claimed-conformant backend profile;
- unsupported semantics -> typed startup refusal;
- no bucket listing participates in truth or recovery;
- adapter dependency surface is registry-approved (no SDK, no Tokio-transitive).

FUTURE-SELF NOTES
If no acceptable real backend exists at decision time, the recorded fallback is building fgit-authorityd (plan D2) — do not weaken the contract to admit a weak backend.

title: FG-007: Transaction seal, stable TxId, and terminal outcome lookup
description:
GOAL

WHY / BACKGROUND
Retry ambiguity is the root pathology of distributed mutation. The seal converts "a network attempt" into "a logical mutation with one stable identity": put-if-absent on canonicalized semantic bytes; byte-identical body -> idempotent retry continuing the same transaction; different body under the same idempotency key -> typed IdempotencyKeyReuse rejection. ## EMBEDDED NORMATIVE CONTENT (verbatim from the design docs; self-contained — do not consult the source markdown)

### TransactionSealBody (NORMATIVE_PROTOCOL_CONTRACTS §5.2) — the exact canonical schema

```rust
struct TransactionSealBody {
    tx_id: TxId,
    tenant_id: TenantId,
    repository_id: RepositoryId,
    authenticated_principal_id: PrincipalId,
    idempotency_key_digest: Digest,
    canonical_request_digest: Digest,
    request_schema: SchemaId,
}
```

The deterministic seal key is scoped by tenant/repository/`TxId`. `put_if_absent(seal_key, body)`:
- absent -> create the stable request-identity body;
- present with matching principal/request/idempotency/schema fields -> retry continues using the existing seal;
- present with any conflicting stable field -> `IdempotencyKeyReuse` rejection.

CRITICAL: admission capability, policy epoch, issuer, and first-seen time are SEPARATE immutable admission receipts over the seal ID; they are NOT seal-body fields, so a legitimate retry never has to regenerate them and byte-identical retry matching stays sound. A seal is durable identity, not a commit or ordering event.

### Terminal outcome (NORMATIVE §5.3)

```rust
enum DecisionOutcome {
    Committed { repository_commit_id: RepositoryCommitId },
    Refused { code: RefusalCode, refusal_record_id: RefusalRecordId },
}
```

Canonical outcome membership lives in the authenticated outcome-index root reachable from the head; direct per-`TxId` pointers and local rows are rebuildable accelerators that cannot contradict the head. A second terminal outcome for one `TxId` is an invariant failure (invariant 2).

### Repository Capsule unsigned body (plan §14.1) — binds at least

repository and security namespace; exact authority-head ID, generation, and version-token evidence class; exact latest decision and committed repository sequences; exact RCR and ref/forge/outcome/retention/outbox/configuration roots; immutable object/segment manifests; graph/search generation roots included in the checkpoint profile; format/crypto/dependency/toolchain registry epochs; durability/placement policy identity; predecessor capsule; backup horizon and replay suffix boundary. A capsule does NOT prove every referenced byte is currently readable, that signatures imply trustworthy code, or that RPO/RTO was met. title: FG-011: FrankenGit Asupersync runtime profile
description:
GOAL
Establish the one final Asupersync runtime/lifecycle profile that every FrankenGit service, FrankenSQLite adapter, gateway, transfer, repair worker, projection, agent, runner, and shutdown path uses.

WHY / BACKGROUND
Asupersync is not merely an executor. Runtime-owned Cx contexts, budgets, four-state outcomes, regions, obligations, deterministic Lab evidence, and native teardown define the concurrency contract. This foundation must precede the embedded FrankenSQLite adapter because its asynchronous API and worker cleanup require the same runtime profile.

STRUCTURE
- implementation child: production context construction, capability narrowing, node AppSpec lifecycle, ownership primitives, budgets/outcomes, obligations, shutdown, and profile identity;
- verification child: deterministic and native cancellation/leak/shutdown/conformance campaigns with detailed evidence.

EPIC ACCEPTANCE
- exactly one Asupersync 0.4.x source/version/feature universe, after the adopted sibling projects complete their upstream convergence work;
- production contexts originate from Runtime/RuntimeHandle request_cx_with_budget APIs, not test/detached constructors; effectful APIs take &Cx first and planted widening attempts fail;
- finite request/child budgets meet inherited deadline/poll/cost/priority constraints; success/error/cancelled/panicked Outcome states remain distinct through policy edges;
- one compiled AppSpec node lifecycle with explicit scope, bounded JoinSet, actor/GenServer, and obligation ownership; no detached authority-bearing work;
- cancellation is request -> drain -> finalize, and dependency-ordered shutdown explicitly closes FrankenSQLite workers before root join;
- verification/release obligation leaks fail fast; any availability recovery mode produces durable containment evidence and escalation; Silent and log-only false quiescence are forbidden;
- deterministic Lab coverage and native parked-worker/file/socket/blocking-worker/process teardown coverage are separately claimed and both pass;
- runtime/profile identity is present in every affected evidence artifact.

NON-CLAIMS
Current actor restart evidence is not a tree-wide compiled-supervisor restart guarantee. Browser/preview primitives are admitted only for their exact supported class. No wrapper may hide Cx, Budget, Outcome, cancellation, or obligation semantics.

REFERENCE
Follow docs/ASUPERSYNC_AND_FRANKENSQLITE_INTEGRATION_PROFILE.md and the dependency constitution. All unit and E2E tests use the shared NDJSON harness and exact release-suite manifest.

---
## PLAN-SPACE REVIEW REVISIONS (added during the pre-implementation polish pass)

### BINDING INTEGRATION PROFILE (§2 Asupersync production profile) — acceptance obligations

Per docs/ASUPERSYNC_AND_FRANKENSQLITE_INTEGRATION_PROFILE.md §2:
- Contexts are created through the owning Runtime/RuntimeHandle via request_cx_with_budget / try_request_cx_with_budget; Cx::for_testing is NOT a production entry point. Every effectful owned API takes &Cx first; a child cannot regain a capability its parent masked. Ambient clock/entropy/env/network/fs/process/secret/billing/publication authority is forbidden inside canonical evaluation.
- Budgets: a child budget is the MEET of parent and requested deadline/poll/cost/priority; code may tighten, never widen. Budget::INFINITE is limited to a named node-root/service-root policy; requests/parsers/transfers/repairs/projection/db/shutdown get finite profile-owned budgets.
- The four-way Outcome (success / domain refusal / cancellation / panic-containment) survives through service internals; at protocol edges cancellation carries commit-ambiguity metadata (resolve the immutable outcome, never report "not committed").
- Ownership shapes chosen by SEMANTICS not convenience: AppSpec node compiled-before-start with a quiescent stop/join; child Scope for fan-out; bounded JoinSet for dynamic homogeneous work; actors/GenServer for stateful protocols; RAII+obligation for resource cleanup. No detached task retains publication/object/db/network/secret/runner/billing authority.
- Obligation-leak policy is configured: verification/release use fail-fast Panic; an availability service may use Recover only with a durable leak record + bounded cleanup + health degradation + escalation; Silent is forbidden and Log alone cannot satisfy closure.
- Shutdown is dependency-aware: stop admission -> cancel -> drain sessions/db commands -> finalize/transfer obligations -> close FrankenSQLite workers explicitly -> flush evidence -> join node root.
- Runtime controls (workers/queues/blocking-pool/stack/parking/scheduler/admission) are named profile inputs; host-derived parallelism is explicit and never accidental replay identity. Do NOT claim a tree-wide compiled-supervisor restart contract the upstream has not proven (per-actor restart only, for now).
- Add acceptance (§5.1): planted capability-widening refused; child-budget meet + exhaustion; four-way outcome + commit-ambiguity mapping; AppSpec ordering + obligation leaks; cancellation at every await with exact request->drain->finalize.

title: FG-025: Conflict witnesses and value-of-information refinement
description:
GOAL
Hierarchical typed conflict witnesses (refs, paths, symbols, policy inputs, forge entities, quota/retention/queue keys) with value-of-information refinement: spend bounded CPU/bytes refining a witness ONLY when expected saved abort cost exceeds refinement cost.

WHY / BACKGROUND
"Different ref names" is a false independence proof (NEG-003): protections, queues, quotas, retention, and forge aggregates overlap across refs. The safe default is the conservative witness; refinement is an OPTIMIZATION with an asymmetric safety rule — refined witnesses may remove FALSE conflicts but never a reference-model TRUE conflict. Sketches (birthday/AMS/HLL-style overlap estimators, inherited from FrankenSQLite) may ESTIMATE overlap to budget refinement but can never prove absence. The semantic rebase ladder (plan section 16.4: revalidate, intent replay, structured patch, merge certificate, refine-then-retry, typed refusal) reuses CAS-loser work deterministically; no byte-level or XOR merge for source state, ever.

STRUCTURE: subtasks = (a) implementation, (b) refinement/starvation evidence.

ACCEPTANCE (epic)
- witness families typed and hierarchical; conservative default always safe;
- refinement decisions receipted (estimated costs, decision, actual outcome);
- deterministic starvation escalation: an old transaction eventually routes through conservative serialized evaluation — statistical estimates cannot deny liveness indefinitely.

## EMBEDDED NORMATIVE CONTENT (verbatim from the design docs; self-contained — do not consult the source markdown)

### Conflict witness families (plan §15.5) — hierarchical and typed; conservative witness is always safe

repository configuration/policy epoch; ref namespace and exact ref value; PR/issue/release aggregate version; merge-queue target and position; path/file/symbol/semantic region; object closure and hidden-ref visibility; quota/retention/legal-hold domain; graph-generation or status-check receipt; authority-head generation. Finer witnesses may prove independence and reduce false aborts but CANNOT weaken correctness (invariant 9: refinement only removes false conflicts).

### Value-of-information refinement (plan §15.6)

```text
expected_saved_retry_cost
  - refinement_cpu_cost
  - refinement_io_cost
  - added_latency_cost
  - uncertainty/risk_margin
```
Only bounded, deterministic, receipt-producing refinement may run. Conflict sketches may predict which refinement is worthwhile; they NEVER authorize admission.

### Semantic rebase ladder (plan §16.4) — after a CAS loss

1. exact witness revalidation with no change; 2. deterministic intent replay on the new basis; 3. structured ref/forge/path patch reapplication with proof; 4. domain-specific append/range/bitmap merge certificate; 5. bounded witness refinement then one of the above; 6. typed retry/refusal/manual merge. There is NO raw byte-level or XOR merge for source state; a source-code text merge is a proposed new intent/evidence object, never a silent change to the sealed request.

title: FG-026: Git TreeFS workspace core
description:
GOAL
The immutable-tree + copy-on-write workspace (crate fgit-treefs): descriptor-relative capability-rooted path API, lazy authorized blob fetch, sparse path sets, overlay intent log, snapshot roots, deterministic materialization, staged/visible/durable workspace epochs, and export to Git objects + a proposed transaction.

WHY / BACKGROUND
A million speculative agent workspaces must be economically different from a million clones (plan section 17.1). TreeFS is capability-scoped by construction: reads fetch only authorized objects; writes are typed TreeEditIntents (Write with entry_class, CreateSymlink, CreateDirectory, RemoveDirectory, Delete, Rename, Chmod, UpdateSubmodule, RecordConflictMarkers, ApplyPatch — the audited-complete variant set in docs/GIT_TREE_FS.md section 7), so every overlay entry kind is producible from a typed intent and the totality map has no unreachable cases. WorkspaceSnapshotBody carries staged_epoch/visible_epoch/durable_epoch (invariant: staged >= visible >= durable). Secrets NEVER persist into overlays — no configuration relaxes this; the exfiltration corpus must detect violations. No ambient sponsor token, host metadata, or unrestricted network.

STRUCTURE: subtasks = (a) core API + overlay, (b) path-security corpus, (c) export + crash replay.

- session points at latest snapshot through a LOCAL anti-rollback record (subordinate authority pattern — not a second truth);
- deterministic materialization: same snapshot yields byte-identical materialized trees.

## EMBEDDED NORMATIVE CONTENT (verbatim from the design docs; self-contained — do not consult the source markdown)

### WorkspaceSnapshotBody (GIT_TREE_FS §2) — exact schema (immutable; a session points to its latest via a local anti-rollback record)

```rust
struct WorkspaceSnapshotBody {
    workspace_id: WorkspaceId,
    repository_id: RepositoryId,
    base_rcr_id: RepositoryCommitId,
    base_commit_oid: GitObjectId,
    base_tree_oid: GitObjectId,
    overlay_root: Digest,
    staged_epoch: WorkspaceEpoch,
    visible_epoch: WorkspaceEpoch,
    durable_epoch: WorkspaceEpoch,
    authorization_root: Digest,
    path_filter_root: Digest,
    toolchain_profile: ToolchainProfileId,
    intent_run_id: Option<IntentRunId>,
}
```
Epoch invariant: `staged_epoch >= visible_epoch >= durable_epoch`.

### TreeEditIntent (GIT_TREE_FS §7) — every §3.2 overlay entry kind is producible from one variant (totality map has no unreachable entries)

```rust
enum TreeEditIntent {
    Write { path, basis_digest, content_id, mode, entry_class },
    CreateSymlink { path, link_target, basis_entry },
    CreateDirectory { path },
    RemoveDirectory { path, basis_entry },
    Delete { path, basis_entry },
    Rename { from, to, basis_entry },
    Chmod { path, before, after },
    UpdateSubmodule { path, before_oid, after_oid },
    RecordConflictMarkers { path, merge_inputs, marker_object },
    ApplyPatch { patch_id, expected_spans },
}
```

### The 11 crash/cancellation interruption points (GIT_TREE_FS §14) — conformance-gated before any related claim advances past proposal

before content reservation; mid-stream write; after body before visible overlay pointer; mid-rename-chain; mid-lazy-fetch; after new objects before repository-transaction publication; (and the remaining staged/visible/durable boundaries). After restart, each intent is ABSENT, VISIBLE in the recovered overlay, or EXPLICITLY REFUSED as incomplete — never a fourth outcome. No orphan mount, process, object-fetch credential, or temporary output survives run closure.

### Secret and path rules (GIT_TREE_FS §12, §15)

Workspace secrets are delivered through brokered handles and are NEVER persisted into the overlay; secret material in overlay content, net effects, or exported Git objects is a policy violation the exfiltration corpus must detect, and no configuration relaxes it. Symlink link-text is DATA (creating a symlink never grants traversal through it); case/Unicode aliases are detected before materialization; prompt text in repository files cannot widen a TreeCapability.

title: FG-029: Canonical forge events and atomic pull-request merge
description:
GOAL

title: FG-030: Minimal Agent Protocol vertical slice
description:
GOAL
One local agent harness end to end: signed/authorized IntentRun with attenuated capability chain, AuthorityReadReceipt, Context Packet, TreeFS workspace, effect-broker obligations, evidence records, and an Evidence-Carrying Change published through ordinary sealed RefTxn semantics.

WHY / BACKGROUND
Agent-native is the product thesis, and its security model is non-textual: repository/issue/web text is DATA and cannot widen capabilities, approve itself, suppress checks, or leak secrets (plan section 26.8). The broker is the only effect path; sponsor authority is never inherited; delegation only narrows. Evidence classes (observed/executed/inferred/statistical/omitted/unresolved) and machine-checked verifier-independence classes make agent claims auditable rather than vibes.

STRUCTURE: subtasks = (a) IntentRun/capabilities/broker, (b) Evidence-Carrying Change + verifier independence, (c) adversarial corpus.

ACCEPTANCE (epic)

---
## EMBEDDED NORMATIVE CONTENT (verbatim from the design docs; self-contained — do not consult the source markdown)

### EffectRecord ledger schema (AGENT_PROTOCOL §effect-broker) — every consequential operation produces one

```text
EffectRecord {
  effect_id, run_id, agent_instance_id, parent_effect_id?,
  capability_id, operation, canonical_input_commitment,
  source_authority_receipt?, budget_reserved, external_idempotency_key?,
  obligation_state, terminal_outcome?, output_commitments[],
  budget_consumed, reconciliation_evidence?,
}
```
"Maybe it happened" is not a valid terminal state for a registered effect; a non-idempotent external API is wrapped by an effect-specific reconciliation protocol.

### IntentRun binding (AGENT_PROTOCOL / plan §26.1)

Binds: sponsor, agent, model/harness, verifier identities; exact repository authority head/RCR/capsule and objective; allowed refs/paths/object/forge/secret classes and network domains; read/write/effect capabilities; CPU/memory/storage/transfer/token/monetary/wall-time budgets; evidence and verifier-independence requirements; expiration/revocation/disclosure/retention policy. The agent receives ATTENUATED authority; sponsor authority is never inherited by default.

### Verifier-independence dimensions (AGENT_PROTOCOL) — typed evidence class, not self-declaration

mutable workspace; credentials and effect authority; model/harness implementation; supplied context and hidden state; oracle/toolchain; operator/organization; human oversight. Policy states which dimensions MUST differ per risk class; a verifier sharing a required dimension yields a typed non-independent verdict / `IndependentVerificationRequired` refusal.

### Prompt-injection boundary (plan §26.8)

Repository/issue/web/package/generated text is untrusted DATA. Text cannot widen capabilities, change base state, suppress required checks, approve itself, disclose secrets, or alter evidence-retention rules. The effect broker and authority protocol are non-textual boundaries.

## EMBEDDED NORMATIVE CONTENT (verbatim from the design docs; self-contained — do not consult the source markdown)

### ReleaseManifestBody (LOCAL_VERIFICATION_AND_RELEASE_PIPELINE) — the signed root-last manifest

```rust
struct ReleaseManifestBody {
    project: String,
    version: SemVer,
    source_commit: GitObjectId,
    source_tree: GitObjectId,
    cargo_lock_digest: Digest,
    constellation_digest: Digest,
    toolchain_fingerprint: ToolchainFingerprint,
```

Every target maps to one unique asset basename, checksum sidecar, optional signature, SBOM, and explicitly listed companion files. GitHub Releases is a distribution adapter reconciled against this manifest, never the source of build truth (NEG-005). Dirty working tree refuses release attempts.

description:

The deterministic authorization/policy engine (plan section 32): compiled content-addressed PolicySnapshots, a declarative bounded policy language, the full protected-ref rule vocabulary, break-glass overrides, and simulation/shadow/warn/enforce rollout modes.

WHY / BACKGROUND
Canonical policy evaluation is deterministic over one named input root (plan 15.9): no wall clock, no unversioned external services, no model output during publication — external checks enter as signed typed evidence receipts with explicit acceptance/expiry rules. ### UI DIRECTION (FINAL -- supersedes every earlier UI-decision note in this bead)

The primary FrankenGit web UI is a familiar, GitHub-like browser application built in a DOM-ORIENTED pure-Rust -> WebAssembly framework (Leptos or Dioxus -- the framework choice is an ADR), server-side-rendered with hydration and styled with Tailwind/CSS.

Why this resolves the UX concerns (the "WASM breaks text selection / a11y / SEO" objection applies to CANVAS-painted WASM like egui/ftui, NOT to this):
- Leptos/Dioxus render the REAL DOM (real elements + real CSS), so text selection, find-in-page, screen-reader accessibility, IME/international input, native scroll, right-click, and SSR/SEO for public repositories all behave like any HTML page. It is NOT a canvas/pixel-painted UI.
- "Looks amazing" is a function of design + Tailwind, not a prebuilt component library; a polished GitHub-like UI is very achievable (more first-party component work than assembling React/shadcn, but the result is as good).
- Performance: WASM's edge is concentrated exactly where a forge is heavy -- large diffs, big file trees, blame, client-side syntax highlighting, franken_markdown rendering, and client-side Merkle-proof verification -- while the chrome costs little either way.

Why pure Rust/WASM over React (given the all-Rust project ethos and the explicit go-ahead):
- One Rust universe end to end: the canonical fgit-codec types, franken_markdown rendering, and the fg037 verified-read verifier are NATIVE modules, not FFI'd into JS. No npm frontend toolchain in the first-party path.

WHY / BACKGROUND
Statistical adaptation without identity is how systems drift into unfalsifiable behavior. title: FG-059: Repository incarnations, rename/delete lifecycle, and migration protocol
description:
GOAL
The identity lifecycle machinery of plan 11.1 and 37.5: typed repository incarnations (delete/recreate under the same owner/name creates a NEW incarnation; nothing stale can revive the prior one), rename/transfer flows, logical-vs-physical deletion states surfaced to users (19.4), and backend/namespace migration as a capsule/authority protocol — never "move the home cell".

WHY / BACKGROUND
Incarnation confusion is a real attack/bug class: stale tokens, caches, federation events, webhooks, or object-location records pointing at a deleted-then-recreated name must NOT act on the new repository. Every canonical record already binds the incarnation ID (fg002 schemas); this bead builds the lifecycle: creation mints an incarnation, deletion tombstones it through retention/grace machinery (fg033), recreation mints a fresh one, and all resolution paths (API, transports, webhooks, caches) check incarnation match. Migration (37.5): repository moves between backends/deployments via export-capsule + restore + conditional routing publication — the routing flip is itself a coordinated decision with anti-rollback, and the source enters a typed read-only-then-tombstone sequence.

- migration drill: export, restore to a second deployment, routing flip, source freeze — client-observable cutover is atomic (old name serves until flip, then redirects/refuses per policy);
- deletion states surfaced distinctly (hidden / tombstoned-in-grace / authorized / deleted-hot / expired-everywhere / crypto-erased).

title: FG-071: Cross-tenant isolation and existence-oracle campaign (invariant 17)
description:
GOAL
Enforce and test normative invariant 17 across storage, cache, index, context, runner, log, and repair domains: one tenant must not learn another tenant's membership or content existence through namespace, authorization, response shape, error class, ranges, dedup, cache, search/graph, repair, or resource-accounting behavior.

PROOF CLASSES
- Deterministic structural controls are the primary claim: tenant/security-domain keyed identities; authorization before lookup/disclosure; indistinguishable forbidden/not-found public responses where policy requires; trust-scoped caches/indexes/repair queues/logs; no raw cross-tenant content key; no shared billing/deletion/key namespace; constant public response schema/size class where declared.
- Timing evidence is a bounded statistical campaign over named hardware, topology, load, sample window, estimator/test, effect-size threshold, power, multiple-testing correction, and seed. It may detect regressions and bound observations for that profile; it does not prove universal timing noninterference or “zero signal.”
- Any residual shared physical resource is explicitly modeled, budgeted/rate-limited, and listed as a non-claim or blocks the relevant hosted profile.

CAMPAIGN
Use at least two mutually unauthorized tenants plus clean same-tenant controls. Probe duplicate uploads, cache warm/cold states, ranges, hidden/missing objects and refs, search/embedding/graph membership, logs/metrics, repair/scrub state, runner/cache artifacts, quota/billing attribution, key rotation, deletion/retention, concurrency, throttling, cancellation, and restart. Randomize/blind trial order; include A/A calibration and a planted raw-content-key or early-existence-check leak that must be detected.

ACCEPTANCE
- structural inspection and production-seam tests show all seven domains use tenant/security-domain identity and authorize before disclosure;
- public observable equivalence is checked for status/error schema, size class, ordering, retry hint, work class, and disclosed metadata for forbidden versus absent cases;
- the predeclared statistical analysis detects the planted leak with required power and finds no effect above the declared practical threshold in clean controls for the exact tested profile;
- a null result is reported as “not detected above threshold in this campaign,” never “zero measurable signal” or a universal proof;
- failures retain raw blinded samples, analysis inputs, environment/load fingerprints, and negative-evidence/revisit record;
- `scripts/e2e/cross_tenant_structural.sh` and `scripts/e2e/cross_tenant_timing.sh` appear exactly once in the release-suite manifest.

E2E LOGGING
Use `set -euo pipefail` and `scripts/e2e/lib.sh`. Emit NDJSON for setup, randomized trial, request, assertion, resource check, analysis, and cleanup with source/toolchain/target/topology/load/runtime/tenant-domain identity, blinded trial/seed, operation and secret-safe parameters, expected/actual public outcome, bytes/work/duration, cache/repair/index class, authority/generation position, effect-size/test/correction/power result, artifact digests, and replay command. Keep raw and unblinded samples access-controlled; preserve logs/state on failure. Final totals separate structural pass/fail, statistical detected/not-detected/inconclusive, unsupported, and skipped; inconclusive/unsupported/skipped are non-pass for a claimed profile.

NON-CLAIMS
This campaign does not establish electromagnetic, global scheduler, co-resident microarchitectural, Internet-scale, or future-hardware timing noninterference unless a separately named isolation profile and oracle cover it.

title: FG-087: Crate-layer (L0-L4) registry and layering-violation checker

LOCAL_VERIFICATION section constitution: "Layering, license-compatibility, and claim-registry checks join this lane as the corresponding machinery lands; they are not implemented yet." It is buildable NOW: plan 43.2 assigns every first-party fgit-* crate to a layer, and verification_lanes.tsv LANE-002 already advertises a dependency/layer report output the checker is expected to produce. title: FG-089: Deterministic worker-budget calculator (shared batch-parallelism policy)
description:
GOAL
The single deterministic worker-budget mechanism franken_markdown contributes (FRANKEN_SUITE_DEEP_DIVE_SYNTHESIS.md:249-251, RESEARCH_PROVENANCE.md:199): worker count as a PURE FUNCTION of CPU cap, memory budget, per-job RSS estimate, mode, and variance — applied uniformly across render, index, graph, pack, repair, and CI workers instead of one-worker-per-core folklore.

WHY / BACKGROUND
"Batch worker count is a pure function of CPU cap, memory budget, per-job RSS estimate, mode, and variance. FrankenGit applies this to render, index, graph, pack, repair, and CI workers instead of 'one worker per core' folklore" (synthesis 5.5). fg027 (doc-lineage) mentions render worker count "derived from declared inputs" for ITS batch, but the doc is explicit that this is ONE shared mechanism spanning six subsystems — and determinism matters: output ordering must be independent of worker count and completion order (synthesis 5.6 complete receipts), so the SAME batch producing the SAME result regardless of how many workers ran is a correctness property, not just a perf tuning. A per-subsystem reinvention would drift (each picking its own heuristic), and non-deterministic worker counts would make batch outputs non-reproducible — breaking replay.

- a fgit-resource (or adjacent) worker-budget calculator: pure fn(cpu_cap, memory_budget, per_job_rss_estimate, mode, variance) -> worker_count, with documented formula;
- the determinism contract: batch output/ordering independent of the returned worker count (a batch run with N=1 and N=many produces identical results);

- calculator is a pure function with unit tests across the parameter space (goldens);
- determinism property: for a fixed batch, output and ordering are byte-identical across worker counts (tested with forced N=1 vs N=max);

description:
GOAL
Generate the Git/API compatibility status ledger FROM executable differential results, per FrankenNetworkX's differential-surface-ledger pattern (FRANKEN_SUITE_DEEP_DIVE_SYNTHESIS.md:371-373) and plan section 18.5 ("Release claims are generated from the executable matrix"): every promised protocol/API symbol or behavior carries a present/partial/missing/unsupported status derived from its oracle corpus, and release compatibility claims are GENERATED, never hand-asserted.

WHY / BACKGROUND
"Every promised protocol/API symbol or behavior has present/partial/missing/unsupported status and an oracle corpus" (synthesis 7.6). Today docs/GIT_COMPATIBILITY_MATRIX.md is HAND-MAINTAINED and the individual differential beads (fg015b/fg016c/fg018c/fg019c object/pack/upload/receive, fg044b merge, fg049 github-compat, fg084 notes, fg085 submodules) each produce verdicts in isolation. Nothing aggregates those verdicts into the matrix status or GENERATES the release claim — so the matrix can silently drift from reality (a row says required-v1/present while its differential corpus is failing or absent), which is exactly the "works with Git is not one boolean" and "the service does not return success for ignored fields" honesty the plan demands. This is the claim-lattice (fg055) applied to compatibility: a compatibility claim advances only when its oracle corpus verifies, and demotes automatically when it regresses.

DELIVERABLES
- a ledger generator: consume the differential-verdict artifacts from all compatibility beads, map each promised symbol/behavior to present/partial/missing/unsupported with its oracle corpus reference and last-verified toolchain/version;
- a staleness/consistency gate: the checked-in GIT_COMPATIBILITY_MATRIX status column must match the generated status (drift fails the docs lane) OR the matrix status is generated outright;
- generated release compatibility claims routed through the fg055 claims machinery (a required-v1 row claimed present with no passing corpus refuses);
- coverage/divergence tracking (which promised behaviors have no corpus yet).

ACCEPTANCE
- the generator produces the status ledger from real differential artifacts on a fixture corpus;
- a seeded regression (a passing row whose corpus is made to fail) flips its status to partial/missing and demotes any release claim depending on it;
- a required-v1 row with NO oracle corpus is flagged (coverage gap), never silently 'present';
- the checked-in matrix and generated status are consistency-gated in the docs lane.

- Generator unit tests over synthetic verdict artifacts; regression/demotion fixtures; e2e scripts/e2e/compat_ledger.sh registered in run_all.sh.

description:

FG-096: Capability-narrow MCP and agent-tool surface
description:
GOAL
Expose FrankenGit's agent-native capabilities through narrow, versioned MCP tools that preserve the same public API, authority, policy, budget, effect, evidence, and cancellation contracts as CLI/web clients. Never provide a generic “execute admin API,” arbitrary shell, raw SQL/storage, or capability-widening tool.

TOOL FAMILIES
Repository discovery; capsule/file reads; authorized search/context; TreeFS workspace; diff/review; CI; PR/issue; evidence; policy explanation; budget; and publication. Each family is independently capability-scoped and can remain typed unsupported until its owning subsystem exists.

STRUCTURE
- FG-096a owns tool/resource/prompt schema and capability/refusal registry.
- FG-096b owns transport/session lifecycle and adapters to generated public APIs/effect broker.
- FG-096c owns schema/conformance, hostile-content/cross-principal, retry/cancellation, and live-client evidence.

EPIC ACCEPTANCE
Every read binds an authorized position/generation and bounded result; every mutation binds canonical parameters, idempotency/seal key, input root, sponsor/delegation chain, budget reservation, and receipt. Repository/tool output is untrusted data and cannot add tools, widen authority, request ambient secrets, approve itself, or suppress gates. Agents can complete the supported workflows without parsing prose or terminal frames. All tests join the exact suite manifest with replayable NDJSON.

FG-098: Planned Git compatibility extensions
description:
GOAL
Preserve five explicitly planned post-v1 Git surfaces as one bounded compatibility cohort, avoiding one-item-per-row tracker theater while keeping every behavior visible: (1) reflog/safety views, (2) LFS locks, (3) signed push certificates, (4) namespaces, and (5) typed sandboxed server hooks.

BOUNDARY
This is subsequent scope and does not block v1 unless a release profile explicitly promotes a member. Each member remains independently supported/partial/unsupported in the executable compatibility ledger. The bead stays open until the selected cohort is implemented with its tests; refusal-only work does not close it.

CAPABILITY CONTRACT
1. Reflogs are deterministic, authorized, rebuildable projections of canonical decisions with source position, retention/legal hold/incarnation semantics, and no mutable authority or GC decision in projection rows.
2. LFS locks are canonical forge intents over exact repo/path/owner/policy bases with stable identity, idempotency, force/break-glass evidence, ordering/pagination, and push/workspace policy integration; LFS object existence is never lock authority.
3. Push certificates preserve bounded exact bytes, nonce scope/freshness/one-use state, registry-approved signature/key evidence, replay protection, and sealed-push policy input; signature validity never grants authorization.
4. Namespaces are typed tenant/repository views binding routing, credentials, seals, refs/objects, caches/indexes/logs/repair/GC/quotas/outcomes; never raw prefixing or another authority head.
5. Hooks are only versioned deterministic admission functions without ambient file/network/process/clock/secrets plus explicitly brokered post-commit effects with obligations/receipts. Arbitrary host scripts remain unsupported.

CODE-UNIT TESTS
Projection rebuild/selectors/expiry/hold; LFS hostile paths and lock races; certificate canonical bytes/nonce/key rotation/replay; namespace traversal/cross-tenant advertisement/reachability/cache/repair; hook determinism/capability/resource/cancel/upgrade. Each positive has a near-identical planted negative for mutable reflog authority, local lock row authority, nonce/policy bypass, shared namespace key, ambient hook access, direct head mutation, partial publication, or silent fallback.

LIVE/DIFFERENTIAL ACCEPTANCE
Run pinned Git/LFS clients where specified, independent structural oracles, cross-tenant controls, crash/cancellation/restart, migration, resource, and teardown campaigns. Claimed cells require exact profile/oracle evidence; unsupported/skipped is non-pass, not a v1 failure unless promoted. The E2E cohort scripts are reflog_view.sh, lfs_locks.sh, push_certificates.sh, git_namespaces.sh, and typed_hooks.sh, each listed exactly once in the profile's suite manifest.

title: FG-103: Stacked-change lifecycle and policy-defined landing
description:
GOAL
Ship subsequent-scope stacked changes as one code-plus-tests forge capability over ordinary Git commits/refs/PRs. Stack metadata is product state, not a proprietary object identity or mutable UI convention.

DELIVERABLES
Stable stack/entry IDs distinct from branch names; exact predecessor/successor DAG with cycle prevention and deterministic order; canonical create/insert/reorder/split/squash/remove/abandon intents; upstack/downstack update and rebase metadata without silently rewriting user commits; exact diff/review-anchor/approval/check inheritance and invalidation per basis; visibility/authorization; target/intermediate movement witnesses; partial versus all-at-once landing policy through FG-083/FG-029; conflict/refusal/recovery; CLI/API/UI/MCP parity and ordinary Git import/export. A stack remains advisory/product state until members land through canonical ref/forge publication.

CODE-UNIT/MODEL TESTS
Acyclicity/order; concurrent edits; stale base/target/policy; review-anchor and approval/check freshness; abandon/delete/rename/incarnation; partial landing/rollback; conflicts; retry/cancel/lost response; authorization; planted stale approval, silent rewrite, cycle, wrong descendant diff, partial RCR, lost/reordered entry, map-order defect.

LIVE ACCEPTANCE
Real Git and public interfaces exercise full lifecycle, large stacks, concurrent author/reviewer/agent/queue actions, target/policy/check movement, conflict and crash/cancel/restart. Reference graph/merge models and Git objects/refs match; all planted defects are caught; evidence freshness and interface parity are exact; landing has one canonical decision per declared batch; no orphan synthetic ref/workspace/check obligation. stacked_lifecycle.sh and stacked_queue_races.sh appear once in the claimed manifest.

E2E LOGGING
NDJSON records source/toolchain/server/client/profile, stack/entry/PR/commit/ref IDs, seed/schedule/failpoint, authority/RCR/policy/check positions, command/exit/duration, expected/actual graph/order/diff/review/landing/refusal, object/ref/receipt/resource digests, and replay. title: FG-104: Deterministic usage and billing evidence ledger
description:
GOAL
Ship subsequent hosted usage/billing as one code-plus-tests capability: exact usage receipts, deterministic pricing epochs, reserve/settle/refund obligations, corrections/disputes, and idempotent external reconciliation. Statistical estimates may forecast or size a reservation; they never silently set a charge.

MANDATORY FIRST ACCEPTANCE — D16 AUTHORITY BOUNDARY
Before code, amend the normative contract to identify the tenant/organization economic authority domain already assumed by plan §§30.3/36/44. It must not compete with RepositoryAuthorityHead for repository truth, use a local FrankenSQLite/projection row or payment provider as authority, or imply cross-domain atomicity. It must specify canonical predecessor replacement/anti-rollback, identities/bytes, ordering, policy and pricing epochs, repository-to-organization usage receipts, cross-domain failure/saga/obligation semantics, recovery/export/migration, and how self-hosted “no billing” profiles refuse/omit it. This decision is not a free-standing close: it is an in-item prerequisite that retires into the normative contract and cannot earn capability credit alone.

DELIVERABLES
Typed hierarchical meter dimensions and exact source receipts; deduplication and conservation; source/toolchain/profile/tenant/org/repo/principal/run identities; fixed-point currency/rounding/tax boundary and effective pricing epoch; preauthorization/reservation with hard maximum, commit to measured use, abort/release unused, adjustment/refund/credit/dispute without history rewrite; invoice/export projections with position/completeness; retention/redaction; idempotent external billing effects and acknowledgement/reconciliation for ambiguous timeouts; provider outage/degraded modes; capability/budget policy and break glass; no secret/card data in canonical logs.

CODE-UNIT/MODEL TESTS
Charge algebra conservation and aggregation; duplicate/out-of-order/missing receipts; rounding/currency/epoch edges; reservation under/over/use/abort; retry/lost response; refund/credit/dispute; pricing/policy movement; provider duplicate/timeout/reversal; crash at every state; tenant/repo move/incarnation; authorization/redaction; planted double bill, estimate-as-charge, local-row authority, provider-as-authority, stale price, negative/overflow, and irreconcilable silent success.

LIVE ACCEPTANCE
Run exact workload receipts through reserve/settle/invoice, cancellation/restart, provider sandbox ambiguity/reconciliation, correction/dispute/refund, tenant isolation and export. Totals reconcile independently from source receipts and external acknowledgements; all planted defects are caught; unresolved provider effects remain visible obligations and nonterminal. billing_conservation.sh and billing_reconciliation.sh appear once in the claimed manifest.

E2E LOGGING
Access-controlled NDJSON records source/toolchain/profile/tenant/org/repo/principal/run, usage/pricing/reservation/effect IDs, seed/failpoint, authority/pricing/policy position, units/rate/rounding/expected/actual money, request/exit/duration, provider acknowledgement class, obligation inventory, artifact/log/receipt digests, and replay. Never log secrets; preserve failed reconciliation state.
